content: 1. Ay J, Bowman J, Campbell E, Freund M, Hodder R, Wolfenden L, et al. conducted a study in 2017 published in the Journal of Adolescence (Volume 57, Pages 74–89) to evaluate the effectiveness of a pragmatic, school-based universal intervention aimed at enhancing student resilience and protective factors to reduce mental health problems in adolescents. 2. Gaete J, Martinez V, Fritsch R, Rojas G, Montgomery AA, Araya R. performed a randomized controlled trial in 2016, published in BMC Psychiatry (Volume 16, Article 276), to assess the impact of a school-based intervention on improving depressive symptoms among at-risk Chilean adolescents. 3. Ismayilova L, Karimli L, Sanson J, Gaveras E, Nanema R, To-Camier A, et al. investigated the mental health outcomes of ultra-poor children in Burkina Faso through a cluster-randomized trial, with findings published in Social Science and Medicine in 2018 (Volume 208, Pages 180–189). 4. Lang JM, Waterman J, Baker BL. conducted a randomized trial in 2009, published in The Journal of Primary Prevention (Volume 30, Issue 5, Pages 587–603), to evaluate the effectiveness of Computeen, a preventive computer and psychosocial skills curriculum for at-risk adolescents. 5. Leventhal KS, Gillham J, DeMaria L, Andrew G, Peabody J, Leventhal S. published a study in 2015 in the Journal of Adolescence (Volume 45, Pages 284–295) on a randomized controlled trial aimed at building psychosocial assets and well-being among adolescent girls. 6. Mendelson T, Tandon SD, O’Brennan L, Leaf PJ, Ialongo NS. reported in the Journal of Adolescence in 2015 (Volume 43, Pages 142–147) on the impact of a trauma-informed school-based intervention designed to integrate prevention into schools. 7. Roberts CM, Kane R, Bishop B, Cross D, Fenton J, Hart B. published a study in 2010 in Behaviour Research and Therapy (Volume 48, Issue 1, Pages 68–73) on the prevention of anxiety and depression in children from disadvantaged schools. 8. Sibinga EM, Perry-Parrish C, Chung S-E, Johnson SB, Smith M, Ellen JM. conducted a small randomized controlled trial in 2013, published in Preventive Medicine (Volume 57, Issue 6, Pages 799–801), to evaluate the effects of school-based mindfulness instruction for urban male youth. 9. Stanton BF, Li X, Galbraith J, Cornick G, Feigelman S, Kaljee L, et al. published a randomized controlled trial in 2000 in the Journal of Adolescent Health (Volume 26, Issue 1, Pages 18–26) to assess the impact of a parental monitoring intervention on reducing parental underestimation of adolescent risk behavior. 10. Velásquez AM, López MA, Quiñonez N, Paba DP. published a study in 2015 in Educational Research and Evaluation (Volume 21, Issue 5, Pages 407–421) on the use of yoga to prevent depression, anxiety, and aggression while promoting socio-emotional competencies in school-aged children. 11. Zandkarimi G, Kamelifar L, Heshmati-Molaee N. conducted a randomized experiment in 2018, published in the Child and Adolescent Social Work Journal, to evaluate the effects of nonviolent communication on reducing stress, anxiety, and depression in young Iranian women. 12. Al-Mohtadi RM, Al-Msubheen MM. published a study in 2017 in the Journal of Education and Practice (Volume 8, Issue 5, Pages 42–49) on the influence of a religious awareness program in reducing death anxiety among children aged 9–12 years in Al Shobak Province. 13. Annan J, Sim A, Puffer ES, Salhi C, Betancourt TS. conducted a community-based randomized controlled trial in 2017, published in Prevention Science (Volume 18, Issue 7, Pages 793–803), to improve mental health outcomes for Burmese migrant and displaced children in Thailand through a parenting and family skills intervention. 14. Puffer ES, Annan J, Sim AL, Salhi C, Betancourt TS. published a randomized controlled trial in 2017 in PloS One (Volume 12, Issue 3, Article e0172611) to evaluate the impact of a family skills training intervention among Burmese migrant families in Thailand. 15. Bahar Z, Ozturk M, Beser A, Baykara A, Eker G, Cakaloz B. published a study in 2008 in Social Behavior and Personality: An International Journal (Volume 36, Issue 1, Pages 123–134) evaluating interventions based on depression sign scores in adolescents. 16. Barron I, Abdallah G, Smith P. conducted a randomized controlled trial in 2013, published in the Journal of Loss and Trauma (Volume 18, Issue 4, Pages 306–321), to assess the effectiveness of a CBT trauma recovery program in Palestinian schools. 17. Berger R, Gelkopf M. published a quasi-randomized controlled trial in 2009 in Psychotherapy and Psychosomatics (Volume 78, Issue 6, Pages 364–371) on a school-based intervention for treating tsunami-related distress in children. 18. Berger R, Gelkopf M, Heineberg Y. conducted a quasi-randomized controlled study in 2012, published in the Journal of Adolescent Health (Volume 51, Issue 5, Pages 453–461), on a teacher-delivered intervention for adolescents exposed to ongoing and intense war-related stress. 19. Berger R, Gelkopf M, Heineberg Y, Zimbardo PA. published a study in 2016 in the Journal of Educational Psychology (Volume 108, Issue 6, Pages 761–771) on a school-based intervention to reduce posttraumatic symptomatology and intolerance during political violence. 20. Betancourt TS, McBain R, Newnham EA, Akinsulure-Smith AM, Brennan RT, Weisz JR, et al. conducted a randomized controlled trial in 2014, published in the Journal of the American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry (Volume 53, Issue 12, Pages 1288–1297), on a behavioral intervention for war-affected youth in Sierra Leone.
